title: Hero looks catalog
description: content/looks.json: the one catalog of hero looks (docs/hero-looks.md §3.1, §6, §7; #664): coats (a colour for one part), specials (whole-figure effects), nameplate frames and titles. Mirrors LookCatalog in packages/shared/src/types/look.ts; where the two disagree, the TypeScript type wins. tools/content/looks-catalog.mjs checks what the schema cannot see: ids unique across all four lists, the plain plate, the starters, every rule naming a real tier, class, campaign or friend, and every frame's art path.

coats.description: Colours for one part of one species (§4, §7.1; #666; two parts, owner 2026-11-07): every species has a main part (look.coat) and an accent part (look.accent), each with its own shelf named for the part. About six starters per part per species, and earned ones. A colour is only ever a colour: whole-figure effects are specials.

part.description: Which of her two parts it colours: main (look.coat; a unicorn's coat, a Bigfoot's fur) or accent (look.accent; a unicorn's mane, a Bigfoot's skin).

specials.description: Whole-figure specials (§5.5; owner 2026-11-07): not colours, every species alike, earned only. sparkle: twinkling sparkles over her, clipped by her figure, still under reduced motion. gilded: her whole figure swapped toward color, keeping its lightness steps, so she reads as a statue of it; her chosen colours are ignored while it is worn.

nameplates.description: Nameplate frames (§7.2), drawn behind the name. The plain plate (id plain) is today's look and has no art.

art.description: Its nine-slice painting, under assets/ (UI art, #665): nameplates/<id>.webp. Drawn once assets/manifest.json -> nameplateFrames.ids lists it as delivered.

titles.description: Titles (§7.3), drawn under the name at 0.6 of its size. Kept short: the longest is what the nameplate collision tests use.

unlock.description: How a look is had (§6): a free starter, a find, or a milestone (a tier, a class rank, a finished campaign, a camp friend, a camp milestone).
